rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Each listed source carries a freshness STAMP, not just a to-do.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L138 horthy-ace-fca stamp reads `[checked:2026-07-31 result:CAVEAT due:asap]`. §11a's own grammar restricts `due:asap` to results in {CORRECT,GONE,NEEDED,STALE}; CAVEAT is not in that set. Its sibling stamp one line above (L137, huntley-context-window) carries the identical result (CAVEAT) but a computed dated due (`due:2026-01-14`) instead — the correct pattern. I re-ran `bash curriculum/evals/scripts/source-freshness.sh --target 2026-09-26 curriculum/lectures/the-loop-half-filled.md` myself (today, not the prior instance's 2026-09-05): huntley-context-window correctly WARNs ('CAVEAT past its own due:2026-01-14 — re-verify or re-stamp'); horthy-ace-fca lands in the INFO bucket as 'accepted caveat' with no WARN at all, confirming the script's own logic treats a CAVEAT-with-due:asap as a permanent exemption, same bucket as due:none/due:cohort. horthy-ace-fca's own prose (L138) names its true anchor ('last substantively edited 2025-12-03'); computed pub+6mo = 2026-06-03 — as of today (2026-09-26) that is roughly 3.5-4 months overdue, i.e. the defect has aged since the last technical verdict, not resolved. The grammar slip is not cosmetic: it is the specific mechanism hiding this source's real staleness from the WARN list a pre-cohort audit reads for actionable debt — the exact harm §11a exists to prevent ('A bare verify-X rots... every cohort re-verifies from scratch').
